question: The idea of Rule of Law in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from which of the following constitutions? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (05/04/2021) Shift 2)
options: Canadian
British
French
German
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is British

Explanation:
The idea of 'Rule of Law' in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the British Constitution. This principle was propounded by British jurist A.V. Dicey. According to Dicey, Rule of Law has three main aspects: supremacy of law, equality before the law, and predominance of individual rights. Article 14 of the Indian Constitution provides for equality before the law, which is a part of the Rule of Law. This principle ensures that no one is above the law and all citizens are treated equally. The concept of Rule of Law is fundamental to the democratic framework of India.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who propounded the Rule of Law? → A.V. Dicey
☛ Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides equality before law? → Article 14
☛ Which feature is borrowed from the British Constitution? → Parliamentary government and Rule of Law
☛ How many aspects of Rule of Law did Dicey mention? → Three
☛ Other names for Rule of Law? → Government by law and supremacy of law
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान में विधि का शासन का विचार निम्नलिखित में से किस संविधान से लिया गया है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (05/04/2021) Shift 2)
options_hi: कनाडाई
ब्रिटिश
फ्रांसीसी
जर्मन
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है ब्रिटिश

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान में 'विधि का शासन' (Rule of Law) का विचार ब्रिटिश संविधान से लिया गया है। यह सिद्धांत ब्रिटिश न्यायविद् ए.वी. डाइसी (A.V. Dicey) द्वारा प्रतिपादित किया गया था। डाइसी के अनुसार, विधि के शासन के तीन मुख्य पहलू हैं: कानून की सर्वोच्चता, कानून के समक्ष समानता, और व्यक्तिगत अधिकारों की प्रधानता। भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 14 में कानून के समक्ष समानता का प्रावधान है, जो विधि के शासन का ही एक भाग है। यह सिद्धांत सुनिश्चित करता है कि कोई भी व्यक्ति कानून से ऊपर नहीं है और सभी नागरिकों के साथ समान व्यवहार किया जाए।

question: Article 51A containing Fundamental Duties was inserted by which constitutional amendment? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (06/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: 44th Amendment
73rd Amendment
42nd Amendment
74th Amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 42nd Amendment

Explanation:
Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment (1976). This amendment was introduced by the Indira Gandhi government during the Emergency (1975-77). It inserted Article 51A, listing 10 fundamental duties for citizens, including respecting the Constitution, national flag and anthem, defending the country, promoting communal harmony, and protecting public property. Later, the 86th Amendment (2002) added an 11th duty to provide educational opportunities for children aged 6-14. The 42nd Amendment is considered the most comprehensive amendment, also adding the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Amendment adding Fundamental Duties → 42nd Amendment (1976)
☛ Total number of Fundamental Duties → Originally 10, now 11
☛ Amendment adding 11th duty → 86th Amendment (2002)
☛ Amendment adding 'Socialist, Secular' to Preamble → 42nd Amendment
☛ Prime Minister during 42nd Amendment → Indira Gandhi
question_hi: मौलिक कर्तव्यों को समाहित करने वाला अनुच्छेद 51A किस संवैधानिक संशोधन द्वारा जोड़ा गया था? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (06/04/2021) Shift 1)
options_hi: 44वां संशोधन
73वां संशोधन
42वां संशोधन
74वां संशोधन
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है 42वां संशोधन

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान में मौलिक कर्तव्यों को 42वें संशोधन (1976) द्वारा जोड़ा गया। यह संशोधन इंदिरा गांधी सरकार द्वारा आपातकाल (1975-77) के दौरान लाया गया था। इसने अनुच्छेद 51A के तहत 10 मौलिक कर्तव्य नागरिकों के लिए जोड़े, जिनमें संविधान का पालन, राष्ट्रीय ध्वज और गान का सम्मान, देश की रक्षा, सामुदायिक सद्भाव को बढ़ावा देना, और सार्वजनिक संपत्ति की रक्षा करना शामिल है। बाद में 86वें संशोधन (2002) द्वारा 11वां कर्तव्य (6-14 वर्ष के बच्चों को शिक्षा के अवसर प्रदान करना) जोड़ा गया। 42वां संशोधन भारतीय संविधान का सबसे व्यापक संशोधन माना जाता है, जिसने प्रस्तावना में 'समाजवादी', 'धर्मनिरपेक्ष' और 'अखंडता' शब्द भी जोड़े।

question: Who among the following publishes the 'Economic Survey' in India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (06/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: Ministry of Finance
NITI Aayog
Central Statistical Organisation
The Reserve Bank of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ministry of Finance

Explanation:
In India, the Economic Survey is published by the Ministry of Finance under the Department of Economic Affairs. It is presented in Parliament before the budget as per Article 112 of the Constitution. The Economic Survey provides an annual review of the country's economy, focusing on growth, inflation, employment, and fiscal policy. The Chief Economic Advisor plays a key role in its preparation. NITI Aayog, the Central Statistical Organisation (now part of Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation), or RBI do not publish the Economic Survey. Hence, the correct option is Ministry of Finance.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When is the Economic Survey presented? → In Parliament before the Union Budget.
☛ Which article mandates the Economic Survey? → Article 112 of the Constitution.
☛ Who drafts the Economic Survey? → A team led by the Chief Economic Advisor.
☛ What does the Economic Survey cover? → Analysis of various sectors and assessment of government schemes.
☛ What is the main objective of the Economic Survey? → To present an annual record of the nation's economic performance.
question_hi: भारत में 'आर्थिक सर्वेक्षण' निम्नलिखित में से कौन प्रकाशित करता है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (06/04/2021) Shift 1)

नीति आयोग
केन्द्रीय सांख्यिकी संगठन
भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक

Solution: सही उत्तर है वित्त मंत्रालय

Explanation:
भारत में आर्थिक सर्वेक्षण वित्त मंत्रालय के आर्थिक कार्य विभाग द्वारा प्रकाशित किया जाता है। यह संविधान के अनुच्छेद 112 के तहत बजट पेश होने से पहले संसद में रखा जाता है। आर्थिक सर्वेक्षण देश की अर्थव्यवस्था की वार्षिक समीक्षा प्रस्तुत करता है और विकास, मुद्रास्फीति, रोजगार तथा राजकोषीय नीति जैसे क्षेत्रों पर ध्यान केंद्रित करता है। मुख्य आर्थिक सलाहकार इसकी तैयारी में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाते हैं। नीति आयोग, केंद्रीय सांख्यिकी संगठन (अब सांख्यिकी और कार्यक्रम कार्यान्वयन मंत्रालय का हिस्सा) या RBI आर्थिक सर्वेक्षण प्रकाशित नहीं करते। इसलिए सही विकल्प वित्त मंत्रालय है।

question: What is the duration of the term of a Rajya Sabha MP? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (06/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: Four years
Five years
Two years
Six years
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Six years

Explanation:
The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Indian Parliament. The term of its members is six years. It is a permanent house and one-third of its members retire every two years. Members of Rajya Sabha are indirectly elected by the elected members of the state legislative assemblies. The President nominates 12 members for their special contributions in fields like art, literature, science, and social service. Rajya Sabha is constituted under Article 80 of the Constitution.

☛ How many members are in Rajya Sabha? → Maximum 250 (245 currently)
☛ Who elects Rajya Sabha members? → Elected members of state legislative assemblies
☛ Number of nominated members in Rajya Sabha → 12 (by President)
☛ How many members retire every two years in Rajya Sabha? → One-third
question_hi: राज्यसभा के सदस्य का कार्यकाल कितने समय का होता है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (06/04/2021) Shift 1)

Explanation:

question: How many schedules are there in Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (06/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: IV
V
VII
VI
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is VI

Explanation:
The Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 of India has a total of 6 schedules. This act was enacted for the protection of wild animals, birds, and plants. Schedule I and II provide the highest level of protection to endangered species. Schedule III and IV include species that are not as critically endangered. Schedule V lists vermin and animals that can be hunted. Schedule VI includes plant species that are prohibited from cultivation. The act also establishes penalties for wildlife crimes and supports the creation of national parks and sanctuaries. It is a comprehensive law aimed at conserving India's biodiversity and preventing poaching and illegal trade of wildlife.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When was Wildlife Protection Act enacted? → 1972
☛ What is in Schedule I? → Endangered species
☛ What is in Schedule V? → Vermin and harmful animals
☛ What is in Schedule VI? → Plant species
☛ What does this act prohibit? → Illegal hunting and trade of wildlife
question_hi: भारत के वन्यजीव संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1972 में कितनी अनुसूचियाँ हैं? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (06/04/2021) Shift 1)

Explanation:

question: Which section of the Constitution of India discusses about the responsibility of states towards international peace and security? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (06/04/2021) Shift 2)
options: Directive Principles of state Policy
Fundamental Duties
Preamble
Fundamental Rights
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Directive Principles of state Policy

Explanation:
Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution contains the Directive Principles of State Policy. Article 51 specifically discusses the responsibility of states towards international peace and security. It directs the state to promote international peace and security, maintain just and honourable relations between nations, and respect international law and treaty obligations. Although these principles are non-justiciable, they are fundamental in the governance of the country. Article 51 reflects the principles of the United Nations Charter and underscores India's commitment to global peace. The Directive Principles aim to establish a welfare state and guide the government in policy-making.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article related to international peace → Article 51
☛ Source of Directive Principles → Irish Constitution
☛ Purpose of Article 51 → Promote international peace and security
☛ Total articles in Part IV → Articles 36 to 51
☛ Nature of Directive Principles → Non-justiciable but fundamental
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का कौन-सा भाग अंतर्राष्ट्रीय शांति और सुरक्षा के प्रति राज्यों की जिम्मेदारी के बारे में चर्चा करता है? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (06/04/2021) Shift 2)
options_hi: राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व
मौलिक कर्तव्य
प्रस्तावना
मौलिक अधिकार
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV (अनुच्छेद 36-51) में राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्वों का उल्लेख है। अनुच्छेद 51 विशेष रूप से अंतर्राष्ट्रीय शांति और सुरक्षा के प्रति राज्यों की जिम्मेदारी पर चर्चा करता है। यह अनुच्छेद राज्य को निर्देशित करता है कि वह अंतर्राष्ट्रीय शांति और सुरक्षा को बढ़ावा दे, राष्ट्रों के बीच न्यायपूर्ण और सम्मानजनक संबंध बनाए रखे, और अंतर्राष्ट्रीय कानून और संधि दायित्वों का सम्मान करे। हालांकि ये तत्व न्यायोचित नहीं हैं, फिर भी ये देश के शासन में मौलिक हैं। अनुच्छेद 51 संयुक्त राष्ट्र चार्टर के सिद्धांतों को दर्शाता है और वैश्विक शांति के प्रति भारत की प्रतिबद्धता को रेखांकित करता है।

question: Which judgment laid the Doctrine of Basic structure of the constitution? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (06/04/2021) Shift 2)
options: Golaknath case
Kesavananda Bharati case
Indra Sawhney case
Shankari Prasad case
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kesavananda Bharati case

Explanation:
The Doctrine of Basic Structure is a fundamental principle of the Indian Constitution. It was established by the Supreme Court in the 1973 Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala case. This judgment held that while Parliament has the power to amend the Constitution, it cannot destroy or alter its basic structure. Before this, the Golaknath case (1967) had ruled that Parliament could not amend Fundamental Rights. Kesavananda Bharati overruled this and introduced the basic structure doctrine. Subsequent cases like Indira Nehru Gandhi case (1975) and Minerva Mills case (1980) further strengthened this doctrine.

☛ What did the Golaknath case hold? → Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights
☛ Which case overruled Golaknath? → Kesavananda Bharati case
☛ What did the Minerva Mills case establish? → Strengthened the Basic Structure Doctrine

question: In which of the following years did the Constitution of India, through the 86th amendment, introduce Article 21-A to provide free and compulsory education to all children in the age group of 6 to 14 years as a Fundamental Right? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (06/04/2021) Shift 2)
options: 2010
2002
2004
2008
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2002

Explanation:
The 86th Amendment to the Constitution of India was enacted in the year 2002. It introduced Article 21-A, making free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for all children in the 6 to 14 years age group. The amendment also modified Article 45 under the Directive Principles of State Policy and added Article 51A(k), which imposes a duty on parents or guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children. This amendment laid the constitutional foundation for the Right to Education Act (RTE), 2009, which came into effect on 1 April 2010.

question: The Vice-President of India is elected by the: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (07/04/2021) Shift 1)

Explanation:
The Vice-President of India is elected by the members of both houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Article 1
Article 10
solution:

Explanation:
Article 3 of the Indian Constitution deals with the formation of new states, alteration of boundaries, change of names, etc. It empowers Parliament to make changes to the boundaries or names of existing states. The process involves the President referring the bill to the concerned state legislature for its opinion, but this opinion is not binding. Article 2 deals with admission or establishment of new states, Article 1 defines the name and territory of India, and Article 10 pertains to citizenship. question: Education is kept under which list of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: State list
Concurrent list
Union list
Government list
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Concurrent list

Explanation:
Education is placed in the Concurrent List of the Indian Constitution. It was transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment in 1976. Subjects in this list allow both the central and state governments to legislate, but in case of conflict, central law prevails. The Concurrent List originally had 47 subjects, but now contains 52 subjects (including education, forests, population control, etc.). This change was made to ensure national uniformity in educational policies across states.

question: Which article of the Indian Constitution talks about 'right to life'? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/04/2021) Shift 1)
options: Article 24
Article 21
Article 23
Article 22
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 21

Explanation:
The right to life is enshrined in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution. It is a fundamental right under Part III and states that 'No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.' It has been termed the 'heart of fundamental rights' by the Supreme Court. Through judicial interpretation, its scope has been expanded to include the right to live with dignity, right to a clean environment, right to privacy, and right to speedy trial. This article imposes a duty on the state to protect the life and liberty of citizens from arbitrary action. It is the most extensively interpreted article of the Constitution.

question: In which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India is it written that 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States'? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (23/07/2021) Shift 1)

Article 3
Article 2
solution:

Explanation:

The Inland Emigration Act, 1859 was enacted by the British to regulate the movement of plantation labourers in colonial India. Under this Act, workers in tea, coffee, and rubber plantations were not allowed to leave the gardens without permission. It was primarily enforced in Assam and Bengal, where British planters needed to ensure a cheap and stable labor force. The Act aimed to prevent labor shortages by binding workers to their contracts, and violators faced punishment. This law effectively restricted the freedom of movement of laborers and kept them tied to the estates. question: The fundamental rights described in the Indian Constitution have been taken primarily from ______. (RPF Constable 2018 (15/02/2019))
options: American Constitution
Constitution of Germany
Constitution of Britain
Constitution of the USSR
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is American Constitution

Explanation:
The Fundamental Rights enshrined in the Indian Constitution are primarily borrowed from the American Constitution. These rights are justiciable and protect citizens from state oppression. Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Indian Constitution includes six fundamental rights: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies. The American Bill of Rights (first 10 amendments) inspired these rights. However, unlike the US, Indian fundamental rights are not absolute; the state can impose reasonable restrictions. The Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) is called the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. This borrowing reflects India's adaptation of global democratic principles to its unique socio-political context.

question: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India examines the accounts of which of the following? (RPF Constable 2018 (15/02/2019))

Neither state government nor central government
Both state and central governments

Explanation:
The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is an independent authority under Article 148 of the Constitution. CAG audits the accounts of the Government of India and all state governments. This includes revenue and expenditure of both the centre and states. CAG also audits accounts of public sector undertakings and other bodies when specified by law. CAG reports are submitted to the President and governors, who then place them before Parliament and state legislatures. This ensures transparency and accountability in the use of public funds. question: Election of Lok Sabha Speaker happens- (RPF Constable 2018 (15/02/2019))
options: By the Chief
By elected members of the Legislative Assembly
Among its members
By the Supreme Court Judges
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Among its members

Explanation:
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is elected by the members of the Lok Sabha from among themselves. This procedure is laid down under Article 93 of the Indian Constitution. The election is conducted by simple majority, and the Speaker presides over the proceedings of the Lok Sabha. To remove the Speaker, a resolution passed by a majority of all the members of the Lok Sabha is required. The term of the Speaker is usually the same as that of the Lok Sabha, but they may continue in office until a new Speaker is elected. The position of Speaker is crucial in Indian democracy as they ensure the impartial conduct of House proceedings.

लोकसभा अध्यक्ष का चुनाव लोकसभा के सदस्यों द्वारा अपने में से किया जाता है। यह प्रक्रिया भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 93 के तहत निर्धारित है। अध्यक्ष का चुनाव साधारण बहुमत से होता है और वह लोकसभा की कार्यवाही का संचालन करता है। अध्यक्ष को हटाने के लिए लोकसभा के सभी सदस्यों के बहुमत का प्रस्ताव आवश्यक है। लोकसभा अध्यक्ष का कार्यकाल आमतौर पर लोकसभा के कार्यकाल के समान होता है, लेकिन वह पद पर तब तक बना रह सकता है जब तक नया अध्यक्ष न चुना जाए। अध्यक्ष का पद भारतीय लोकतंत्र में महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि वह सदन की कार्यवाही को निष्पक्षता से संचालित करता है।
